verdict.rationale: ADK's own docs say agents can be packaged as containers and run in any container environment. They describe an option for running offline or in a system with no connection to Google Cloud, and the CLI ships `adk deploy docker` for local deployment. Model adapters cover locally running models, which removes dependence on Google's hosted models. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of a fully self-hosted deployment, and detail on how local-model adapters and supporting services are configured without Google Cloud.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can run my agents entirely on my own infrastructure with no dependence on the vendor's platform

citations.quote: This is a good option if you prefer to run offline or disconnected, or otherwise in a system that has no connection to Google Cloud.
You can manually package your Agent into a container image and then run it in any environment that supports container images.
Deploying the Agent Locally with Docker Container:
we provide adapters that let you connect with many other models and model providers, including locally running models.
